Sourcesrc/core/tokens/starfield/params/spiral.ts
UX surfaceShared primitives every surface builds on — no direct UI.

Members

COUNT_MAX

Per-galaxy particle count ceiling — spiralDisc.count may ask less.

MOBILE_DIVISOR

Mobile particle divisor — caps GPU buffers on small viewports.

MOBILE_WIDTH

Viewport width (px) below which the mobile divisor applies.

VOLUMETRIC_OPACITY

Volumetric galaxies (the Milky Way) are viewed from inside — keep the particle layer faint and thin so it reads as a stellar disc/band instead of an opaque glowing ball that fills half the screen.

VOLUMETRIC_PX

Near-field point size (world units) — the floor while the camera is embedded in the disc. When the camera pulls back, updateGalaxyClouds grows the size linearly with distance so every point keeps at least VOLUMETRIC_PX_SCREEN screen pixels — real stars are point sources whose apparent size floors at one pixel, so the spiral arms resolve from outside instead of vanishing into sub-pixel dust.

VOLUMETRIC_PX_SCREEN

Minimum apparent point size (device px) once the camera leaves the disc. The shared soft-glow map keeps only ~1/3 of a point's sprite lit, so this is set well above 1px for the lit core — not the sprite edge — to stay resolved at galactic range.

VOLUMETRIC_FAR_GAIN

Far-field opacity gain — as the camera pulls clear of the disc the fade drives opacity from VOLUMETRIC_OPACITY up to VOLUMETRIC_OPACITY·(1+GAIN), so the spiral's arms read at galactic range where 400k points would otherwise thin into a uniform wash.

VOLUMETRIC_ARM_JITTER

Arm angular jitter (rad) for the embedded volumetric disc — tighter than photo-fallback spirals because the whole 400k-point field must carry the arm lanes alone (no imagery underneath to do the work).

VOLUMETRIC_HALO

Stellar-halo fraction for the embedded disc — a small spherical globular-cluster population around the core gives the third spatial level (bulge → disc → halo) the flat disc alone lacks.

VOLUMETRIC_COUNT_MAX

Volumetric particle ceiling — spiralDisc.count may ask less.

INNER_SPIN_R

Rotating inner-disc fraction (× radius) — volumetric galaxies split their particle fill at this radius: the inner region carries the spin revolution around the galactic centre while the outer disc (which contains the carved heliocentric bubble) stays put so the Sun's exclusion zone never sweeps stars through the solar system. Real galactic rotation is differential anyway — inner material laps the rim, so a spinning core inside a still outer disc is the honest read. 0.3 keeps the rotors well inside the Sun's 0.51 ring.

ROTOR_DIFF

Differential-rotation factor — the inner-disc rotor spins at ROTOR_DIFF× the whole-disc rate inside the rotating frame, so the core laps the rim the way real flat rotation curves do (inner material completes more revolutions per unit time).

DUST_COUNT

Volumetric dust lanes — the Great Rift. Large soft dark points laid along the arm gaps with NORMAL blending so they absorb the lit disc behind them; additive blending can't darken, so dust gets its own cloud at a fraction of the star budget.

DUST_PX

Dust point size (world units) — fat soft occluders, not pinpricks.

DUST_OPACITY

Dust alpha — high enough to visibly rift the band, low enough to keep it translucent.

DUST_R_MIN

Lane bands sit at these radius fractions of the disc.

DUST_JITTER

Lane angular scatter (rad) around the mid-gap line.

DUST_R

Dust grain color — near-black with a warm cast (dust reddens).

GOLDEN

Golden-ratio spiral geometry — real galactic arms are logarithmic spirals, and a log spiral whose radius grows by φ per quarter-turn has the constant golden pitch atan(2·ln φ/π) ≈ 17.03°. ARM_LOG_B is that spiral's θ-coefficient (θ = B·ln r) so arm curvature follows the same Fibonacci growth seen in phyllotaxis instead of a linear wind; ARM_LOG_R0 is the nominal arm-origin radius (θ = 0 there, just outside the bulge) and ARM_LOG_RMIN floors the log so bulge-overlapping points wrap gracefully rather than diverging.

GOLDEN_ANGLE

Golden angle ≈ 137.5° (2π·(2−φ)) — the divergence angle that keeps successive structures maximally non-repeating; phases the arm sway and spur offsets so no two arms share a rhythm.

ARM_PITCH_TIGHT

Pitch tightening — ARM_LOG_B keeps the golden reference value (the spiral whose radius grows by φ per quarter-turn, pitch ≈17°). The applied winding multiplies it by this factor: <1 loosens the arms (fewer turns, bolder sweeps), >1 coils them. 0.85 lands the Milky Way at ~0.9 turn per arm — arms that sweep instead of stacking into ring-grooves (≥1.4 turns reads as concentric circles).

ARM_PITCH_VAR

Per-arm pitch variation — each lane winds at its own rate: the golden coefficient is perturbed by ±ARM_PITCH_VAR with a golden-angle phase per arm index, so no two arms draw as parallel copies (real spirals are asymmetric — the MW's Perseus and Scutum–Centaurus arms have measurably different pitch angles).

ARM_LUM_VAR

Per-arm luminance variation — deterministic dimming per arm index (golden-angle-keyed sinusoid in [0,1]) so arms differ in brightness the way real major/minor arm pairs do instead of identical stripes.

ARM_SWAY_FREQ

Arm path wobble — a slow sinusoidal sway on the arm angle (freq·radius ≈ 2.5 full waves, each arm phase-offset by the golden angle) so arm lanes meander like real flocculent spirals instead of drawing as perfect geometric curves.

ARM_SWAY_CORE

Sway radius scaling — arm meander starts at ARM_SWAY_CORE× the amplitude near the bulge (the inner disc is resonance-locked, so its lanes run smoother) and reaches full amplitude at the rim where flocculent turbulence dominates.

KNOT_LOBES

Star-forming knots — per-point brightness modulation along each arm (azimuthal lobes drifting with ln r) breaks uniform lanes into glowing OB-association/H-II clumps; KNOT_DEPTH is the max dimming.

KNOT_POW

Sparse hot-knot shaping — max(0, sin)^KNOT_POW isolates discrete star-forming regions along a lane (a high exponent turns the continuous ripple into separated bright clumps instead of a smooth wave); KNOT_HOT_* is the additive blue-white emission those OB associations and H-II nebulae contribute on top of the arm color.

HII_FRAC

H-II region tint + fraction — HII_FRAC of hot knots glow hydrogen-alpha pink instead of OB blue-white, the emission-nebula beads real spiral arms are strung with (Orion, Eta Carinae, M8/20).

BAR_X

Galactic bar — the Milky Way is a barred spiral: bulge points stretch ×BAR_X along a seeded in-plane axis (each galaxy's tilt is derived by a golden-fraction hash of its seed — no extra RNG stream, so worker/local parity is preserved).

LANE_MIX

On-lane blue shift — points near an arm's spine (small scatter draw) blend toward this blue-white tint, the young disc population real spirals show along their arms; scattered inter-arm points keep the warm ramp. LANE_SCATTER_INV normalizes the three-die scatter draw (range ±1.5) to a 0–1 lane distance.

LUM_JITTER

Per-point luminance grain — ±LUM_JITTER brightness scatter (drawn from a triangular distribution so most points sit near the mean) keeps arm lanes granular like resolved stellar populations rather than a painted uniform stripe.

DISC_SPREAD

Disc overshoot + rim dissolve — arm points spread to radius×DISC_SPREAD while brightness rolls to zero from EDGE_FADE_START outward, so the disc edge vaporizes into intergalactic dark instead of cutting a hard ring.

DISC_FLARE

Disc flare — the real Milky Way's gas/star disc flares outward: vertical thickness grows linearly with radius (~1 + DISC_FLARE at the rim), which is what gives the edge-on view its rising wedge instead of a constant-thickness ribbon.

DISC_WARP

Disc warp — the outer disc bends out of the midplane (the MW's integral-sign warp, ~3 kpc at the rim). Amplitude is a fraction of disc radius applied at (r/R)² · sin(angle − warpPhase); the phase is perpendicular to the bar, matching how the real warp sits roughly orthogonal to the bar's long axis.

ARM_JITTER

Arm angular jitter (rad) on photo-fallback spiral fills.

ARM_JITTER_CORE

Organic arm scatter — real spiral arms hold together at the core and dissolve into flocculent wisps at the rim. The per-point jitter is scaled from CORE×jitter at r=0 to RIM×jitter at r=radius, and ARM_SPUR_FRAC of disc points drop into the inter-arm gaps with an extra ARM_SPUR_JITTER spread — the branching feather lanes between main arms that keep the pattern fibrous instead of geometric.

BULGE

Fraction of points inside the central bulge (rest go to the arms).

CORE_PHOTO

Core-glow sprite opacity over the photographic disc (whisper bloom).

CORE_GLOW

Core-glow sprite opacity on the procedural fallback disc.

CORE_R

Per-point color ramp — hot amber bulge → dusty pale-violet rim, matching the real Milky Way's warm dust lane palette (pure blue edges read as a grey fog from inside the disc).

HALO_RADIUS

Stellar-halo radius (× disc radius) for spiralDisc.halo layers.

HALO_DIM

Halo brightness floor — real stellar halos are ~1% of the disc's light; undimmed points render as a giant fuzzy ball that washes out the arms. Multiplies every halo vertex's color.

ELLIPSE_RADIAL

Elliptical-dwarf distribution — radial profile length (× radius), vertical squash, and the core→rim brightness ramp.

ELLIPSE_EDGE

Rim fade start — fraction of the filled volume's outer extent where per-point brightness begins its smooth roll-off to zero. Without it the density cutoff reads as a hard ball boundary instead of a haze that dissolves into the sky.

DWARF_HALO_SCALE

Dwarf-galaxy backing glow — spiralDisc.elliptical bodies carry no photographic disc, and their size-attenuated star Points collapse to sub-pixel specks at Local-Group standoff distances, so a soft tinted halo sprite the size of the whole smudge keeps dwarfs readable as fuzzy unresolved patches from across the group.

SUN_BUBBLE

Heliocentric exclusion bubble (chart units) carved out of a spiralDisc.bubble galaxy's particle fill around the solar system — keeps random disc stars from overlapping the Sun/planet meshes while staying far smaller than the ~267-unit galactocentric gap, so the Sun still reads as embedded in the disc. Sized past the shrunken Kuiper edge (~30 units under SOLAR_SCALE) with margin.

BUBBLE_KEEP

Local-bubble sparsity — the carved neighborhood isn't truly empty (the real Local Bubble is underdense, not hollow): BUBBLE_KEEP of in-bubble points stay at BUBBLE_DIM brightness, so the solar region shows a sparse faint scatter instead of a scrubbed hole.

SEED_STEP

Per-point Fibonacci hash step — the Knuth multiplicative constant 2³²/φ scatters sequential point indices across the seed space so each vertex owns an independent deterministic LCG stream. That makes every buffer fill partitionable by index range — the same job runs chunked across the multi-worker WASM pool on several threads and bit-identically in the main-thread fallback.
